newsitem.title: USA: Tosco fire makes US gasoline market curious.
newsitem.headline: Tosco fire makes US gasoline market curious.

text.p: The fire and shutdown at Tosco Corp's fluid catalytic cracker at its refinery in New Jersey has done little to lift prices but much to raise the market's level of curiosity as to how long the unit will be down.

Some traders said Tosco may have been spotted early Thursday looking for an estimated 50,000 barrels of "A5" regular 87-octane reformulated gasoline (RFG) in New York Harbor, but that could not be immediately confirmed.
Other traders said Tosco had dipped into NYMEX gasoline markets for some spread trading aimed at hedging its exposure to the outage, buying January and selling February contracts.

But traders mostly had questions about the outage, noting the outage would have to be sustained given widespread views the East Coast market is scheduled to receive voluminous cargoes of imported gasoline for the rest of the month.
"It's a little too early for prices to start moving. We'll just have to see what (Tosco) says about it," said one trader.
The NYMEX, bearing the brunt of bullish reaction to the Tosco news, was itself late Thursday morning coming off its earlier highs.
"There's not much change out there. It's really very quiet," another spot trader said.

Gasoline prices stood about 0.70 cent a gallon higher due to the NYMEX move, but differentials were steady, as some views early Thursday that cash differentials were strengthening failed to materialize.
But diffs on prompt "A5" regular reformulated gasoline stood at between 1.00 cent and 1.25 cents over January NYMEX unleaded, meaning the NYMEX was doing all of the upside work.
Wednesday night's fire was located in a safety valve but was quickly extinguished, according to an industry source who noted an extraordinary emission of catalyst coated a nearby neighborhood.
The Bayway refinery, the crown jewel of Tosco's operations, is dubbed the "gasoline machine" by traders due to the prolific gasoline output at the plant.
The downed cat cracker, the world's largest, can process 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) of feedstock, while the whole refinery has crude distillation capacity of 290,000 bpd.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
